summary: This diff adds three new files from a red-team review run on a Redis session-cache design: grading.json, charter.md, and metrics.json. grading.json records that all 9 grading expectations passed (12 findings ranked 1-12, sizing math, stale-price windows, KEYS-based invalidation risk, a verdict with a minimum-changes path, and coverage beyond the planted flaws), plus a claims list, execution metrics, timing notes, uncertainties/workarounds, and eval-feedback suggestions for improving the grading criteria. charter.md defines the review's scope: the artifact under review, four ranked harm categories (wrong prices, Redis cluster meltdown, checkout latency collapse, silent failure), out-of-scope items, and a success criterion. metrics.json duplicates the tool-call and output-size figures already present in grading.json's execution_metrics block.

claims.text: All 9 grading expectations passed (passed=9, failed=0, total=9, pass_rate=1.0)
F-3 (KEYS-based invalidation, rank 3) is ranked above every Plausible/conditional finding, and F-1/F-2 above it are shown as unconditional or reasoned to hold under every branch
The design's Invalidation section handles only the promo_changed event; catalog and tax changes have no invalidation path
The design specifies KEYS session:*:pricing then DEL on a Redis cluster shared with rate limiting and feature flags
Cache key includes session ID only, cited as the basis for findings F-6 and F-8
Rollout is a single jump from 5% to 100% after a day, gated by feature flag cache_pricing_v1
12 raw findings, 1 merge, 1 seam-sweep addition, 0 killed, yielding 12 final findings
Two adversaries independently hit the stampede root cause (F-4 corroboration)
charter.md ranks four harm categories: wrong prices, shared Redis cluster meltdown, checkout latency/availability collapse, silent failure
metrics.json reports the same tool_calls, total_tool_calls, output_chars, and transcript_chars values as grading.json's execution_metrics block

risks.note: metrics.json restates the identical tool-call counts and character totals already embedded in grading.json's execution_metrics field, as two copies of the same data with no indicated source of truth.

The claim about raw/merged/seam-swept finding counts is marked verified:true, but its own evidence text says it 'cannot be independently confirmed without a transcript' -- the verified flag is stronger than the evidence backing it.

least_confident: Whether marking the '12 raw findings, 1 merge, 1 seam-sweep' claim as verified:true is justified, since the chunk's own evidence text for that claim says it cannot be independently confirmed without a transcript.
